title: Google Messages Redesign Introduces Pinned Avatars, Bottom Search, and Gemini Corner Feature
body:
Google is rolling out a substantial redesign of the Messages app’s home screen for Android users, introducing a new visual identity, reorganised chat navigation, a bottom‑aligned search bar, and a prominent Gemini AI shortcut. The changes, currently being tested on a limited set of devices, aim to streamline conversations, surface important contacts, and integrate Google’s generative‑AI capabilities more directly into everyday messaging.

The most noticeable alteration is the fresh app icon, which adopts a minimalist speech‑bubble silhouette in Google’s signature palette, signaling a shift toward a cleaner, more modern aesthetic. Beyond cosmetics, the overhaul reshapes the way users interact with their chats. A new “Pinned Chats” section now appears at the top of the conversation list, allowing users to anchor up to three threads for quick access. Unlike the previous implementation where pinned chats were interspersed among recent messages, the dedicated strip ensures that high‑priority contacts—family members, work groups, or ongoing projects—remain constantly visible.

Another core component of the redesign is the relocation of the search function from the top of the screen to a bottom‑center position, mirroring the layout popularised by many contemporary mobile apps. The bottom‑aligned search bar is larger, with rounded corners and a subtle microphone icon, encouraging both typed and voice queries. This move not only aligns with Google’s broader design language across its suite of services but also makes the search field reachable with a thumb, improving ergonomics on larger phones.

Perhaps the most forward‑looking addition is the integration of Gemini, Google’s generative‑AI engine, directly into the Messages home screen. A small, animated Gemini icon sits in the lower‑right corner, offering users instant access to AI‑driven suggestions, quick replies, and contextual information without leaving the conversation view. Tapping the icon can generate draft replies, summarize lengthy threads, or even pull in relevant web content, effectively turning the messaging app into a hub for AI‑enhanced communication.

Industry analysts see the redesign as part of Google’s broader strategy to embed AI more deeply into its core products, competing with rivals that have already introduced AI‑powered features in messaging platforms. By placing Gemini at the forefront, Google not only showcases the technology’s capabilities but also gathers real‑world usage data that can refine the model’s performance in conversational contexts. The redesign also reflects a response to user feedback that the previous home screen felt cluttered and that important chats could get lost amid a flood of notifications.

Early testers have reported mixed reactions. Many appreciate the clarity brought by the pinned chats bar and the thumb‑friendly search placement, noting that it reduces the time needed to locate a specific conversation. However, some users expressed concern that the new layout reduces screen real estate for the message list itself, especially on devices with smaller displays. Additionally, the Gemini shortcut, while innovative, raises questions about privacy and data handling, prompting Google to reiterate that AI processing occurs on-device where possible and that user consent is required for any data sent to the cloud.

Google has not yet confirmed a rollout schedule, but the company typically expands successful experiments to a broader audience over several months. If the redesign proves popular, it could become the default experience for the next major version of Messages, aligning the app with Google’s vision of an AI‑first mobile ecosystem. As the testing phase continues, users can expect further tweaks—such as adjustable pin limits or customizable AI suggestions—based on the feedback collected. The upcoming months will reveal whether the new design will set a new standard for Android messaging or prompt Google to revisit its approach.
